chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi from Muhammad ibn Walid from Umar ibn Yazid who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say, 'The joining (of circuits) is disliked only in the obligatory [prayer]; as for the optional [prayer], by Allah, there is no harm in it.'

key_terms.الْقِرَانُ: Joining two circuits of Tawaf without resting between them

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to join two circuits of Tawaf without resting during optional prayers?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the obligatory and voluntary aspects of Tawaf prayers, ruling that while joining circuits (*Al-Qiran*) is disliked during the mandatory Fajr prayer, it is entirely permissible during voluntary prayers. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly principle that the strictures of obligatory acts do not necessarily extend to their voluntary counterparts, offering flexibility for pilgrims. The narration underscores the practical ease Islam provides in worship, allowing believers to maintain continuity in their devotional acts without unnecessary interruption.
